title: Selected Nancay visits show no clear link between burst rate and typical fluence in FRB 20220912A
abstract: We test whether typical burst fluence falls as detected activity rises in FRB 20220912A. Public Nancay data give 621 episodes in 36 visits with at least three episodes. An equal-visit log-log fit with separate 30-day intercepts gives slope -0.040, a nominal 95 percent visit-bootstrap range of -0.241 to 0.115, and a conditional mark-permutation p-value of 0.6656. Six threshold, sample-size and time controls retain ranges that include zero. A direct least-squares check and an exact small permutation check pass. This is a null result for a geometric-mean statistic and selected detected rates. It does not exclude a fixed-power emission model: rate error, incomplete detection, changing spectra and a changing fluence distribution can hide the relation. There is no independent telescope test or new physical detection. Code, source hashes, retrieval instructions, aggregate results and a figure support reproduction.

display.caption: Between-visit log-log slopes and nominal 95 percent visit-bootstrap ranges. All tested ranges include zero. The -1 reference needs a fixed-power, fixed-shape scale model.
